sourceBindings.text: The same schematic crucible moves between weighing, a closed furnace and controlled cooling. Its contents and sizes are illustrative, not a calibrated sample or operating instructions. No real temperature, timer or furnace controls are provided.

A qualified trainer conducts any real drying, ignition, cooling and weighing under the local laboratory procedure. The student observes, records the stated masses and explains the calculation. The online exercise uses invented masses and grants no independent hot-equipment competence.
Record the clean, dry empty crucible: C
Add oven-dry soil and record the combined mass: D
Qualified operator performs ignition under the laboratory method
Qualified operator completes controlled cooling
Record the cooled crucible plus residue: I
Sequence correct. The laboratory supplies its full method; watching this sequence does not qualify you to handle hot equipment.
Editable high-contrast masses, formula in text, keyboard-capable ordering and narration that reads symbols without depending on colour.

sourceBindings.text: Learner orders and explains empty crucible, oven-dry soil plus crucible, controlled ignition, safe controlled cooling and final mass, and identifies the site's method and qualified operator as necessary.
Pass for a correct explanation and safety boundary; the student does not receive furnace-operation competence from watching a demonstration.
Learner computes dry soil mass and post-ignition loss with crucible cancellation, then divides loss by dry soil mass. In the declared example: (35.00−34.75)/(35.00−30.00)×100 = 5.0% LOI.
Pass only with correct denominator, arithmetic, percent unit and explicit illustrative-data label; a percentage without method or masses is insufficient.

Learner states that residual moisture, clay-bound water or other nonorganic mass loss can affect LOI depending on method and soil; interprets 3–6% only as a classroom example and asks for local soil, climate and laboratory context.
Pass with at least one correct interference and one site/method limitation. Calling the result exact OM or declaring all soils outside 3–6% unhealthy does not pass.
